previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of post-polio syndrome, osteoporosis, and coronary artery disease was admitted for acute worsening of chronic lower back pain and new bilateral great toe numbness. MRI revealed acute to subacute compression fractures at L3 and L5, an acute on chronic fracture at L2, and a severe chronic L1 fracture with spinal canal narrowing. Neurology and neurosurgery recommended conservative management with a TLSO brace, pain control, and rehabilitation. She was started on iron for low ferritin contributing to restless legs and continued on home medications for CAD and hypothyroidism. Urinary symptoms were chronic and not infectious. She was discharged to extended care for inpatient rehabilitation with follow-up planned in spine and cardiology clinics.

# Acute T12 Vertebral Compression Fracture 
# Osteoporosis
Patient admitted with back pain that radiated around her sides, 
with CT scan in ED demonstrating new T12 vertebral compression 
fracture.  Patient was seen by ortho spine, who recommended TLSO 
brace and non-operative management.  Patient was fitted for TLSO 
brace, had repeat imaging that was reassuring, and was seen by 
physical therapy who recommended rehab.  Course notable for 
patient being resistant to wearing TLSO--discussed with 
ortho-spine who recommended she wear it whenever she is out of 
bed to help healing and prevent neurologic damage.  Continued 
outpatient Tylenol+codeine ___ checked).  Continued calcium 
+ vitamin D--defer additional management to outpatient setting. 
Scheduled for ortho spine follow-up at 2 weeks.

# Urinary frequency
Patient reported urinary frequency on presentation without 
dysuria, leukocytosis, or fevers.  UA and urine culture 
suggestive of contaminant.  Patient had been given antibiotic in 
ED, but these were stopped on admission.  Given recurrent 
symptoms, repeat UA was sent which did not demonstrate signs of 
infection.  Teaching was done with patient that urinary 
frequency may not mean an infection is present.  Encouraged 
patient to follow-up with outpatient urology for workup of her 
symptoms. 

# ___ Colitis 
Patient course notable for onset of diarrhea following 
admission.  Cdiff PCR was positive.  Suspect patient was 
predisposed to Cdiff secondary to recent outpatient course of 
antibiotics and those given in the ED as well.  On PO 
vancomycin, patient's stool frequency and quantity decreased and 
patient reported symptomatically feeling improved also.
